chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Usamah bin Zayd: 'O Usamah, do not intercede regarding a Hadd (penalty).'

key_terms.أُسَامَةُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ: Usamah bin Zayd, a companion of the Prophet
key_terms.تَشْفَعْ: To intercede or plead on behalf of someone
key_terms.حَدٍّ: Fixed divine penalty or punishment prescribed in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: Can one intercede to reduce a fixed Islamic penalty (Hadd)?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, highlights the distinction between general intercession and specific legal penalties by citing the Prophet's instruction to Usamah bin Zayd, a figure of high status and kinship, to prevent him from waiving a fixed divine punishment (Hadd). In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes that while intercession is possible, it does not nullify the objective reality of the Hadd itself, preserving the integrity of divine law against arbitrary political or social influence.
